page: Microsoft Azure E48s_v4 is an ESv4-family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 24 physical Intel Xeon 8370C cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base speed of 2.8 GHz and includes 35 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results indicate strong memory performance, with uncached read-only large block memory bandwidth reaching 250.5 GB/sec and uncached write large block bandwidth at 126.78 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25 percent. Most other compute metrics fall into the average range, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1435.0 and a multi-core score of 13756.0. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression is a notable bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25 percent at 8.79 GB/sec, whereas multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches an average tier of 69.71 GB/sec. Large-model LLM inference is also weak, with 70B model prompt processing limited to 6.57 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E48s_v4 offers high memory density relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. Given the 384.0 GB RAM capacity and average database operation benchmarks of 16099.44 on Passmark, this server is suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and enterprise applications requiring substantial memory footprints without intensive parallel GPU computation.
